utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution would like to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. There are a few matters this morning. First, with respect to RM509, the Prosecution owes the Chamber a decision on whether we will call that witness. I want to inform the Chamber of the Prosecution's decision with respect to the need to adduce the evidence of RM509. In short, the Prosecution does not intend to call this witness with the caveat which I will explain below given that there is a small chance that it may still be necessary to call him to establish the foundation for two intercepts. Your Honour, the next bit of my submission requires or -- private session because it deals with a protected witness, so I'd ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, now with respect to RM247, the Chamber provisionally admitted the evidence of RM247 pursuant to 92 bis on the 6th of September, 2013. The Prosecution has decided to move to withdraw this witness because during the attestation process the witness provided inconsistent information on one aspect of his statement. We have already provided information about this to the Mladic Defence pursuant to Rule 68. If the Chamber will entertain an oral motion to withdraw him, we would do that, or if the Chamber would prefer that it be done in writing, we would do that in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it can be done orally, even on the spot. I do understand that you withdraw the motion to have the evidence of Witness RM247 to be withdrawn from the 92 bis application.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a look at it, but most likely we'll give a very short oral decision. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this next application addresses two -- two intercepts, 65 ters 20873 and 28036, and I've spoken to Mr. Lukic about this so he knows that I'm making this application. On 19th of September, the Chamber entered its decision on the admission of evidence related to RM506 [Realtime transcript read in error "RM5067"]. At that time, the Chamber inquired about the tendering of the same item of evidence with duplicate 65 ter numbers, and that is 65 ter 2873 [sic] and 28036. The Prosecution has reviewed the -- the Chamber's comments about these two exhibits, and now withdraws the tendering of 20873 and re-tenders, 28036. As the Chamber correctly pointed out there are differences in the English translations, although the B/C/S text is the same. The Prosecution relies on 28036 as this exhibit has the official CLSS translation and the other was a draft translation. Additionally, the Chamber inquired about the difference in the number of the heading of the intercept. The Prosecution submits that these two numbers reflect that the intercept was entered twice in the bookkeeping system for intercepts and relies on RM506's general explanation of the meaning of these heading numbers as -- as mentioned in his testimony. So the -- at this time, the Prosecution tenders 28036.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, on page 4, line 4, a number, "2873," appears, may I take it that you intended to say or even have said "20873."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we also have on page 4, line 2, a "Witness RM5067" and that should be "RM506," I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the question that remains is, is there any objection against admission of 28036?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Mr. Groome informed me this morning about this issue, but we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we didn't have time to check. Probably we wouldn't have any objections, but we have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we hear from you not later than this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next issue is a request from the Prosecution for the Chamber to clarify a recent decision on the Prosecution's 18th Rule 92 bis motion entered on the 23rd of 2013, with respect to the witness, Mirsad Krlic. In paragraph 7 of the decision, the Chamber states that the Witness Krlic's attestation in his testimony in the Krajisnik case meets the attestation requirement of Rule 92 bis B. However, in paragraph 15, the Chamber instructs the Prosecution to file the corresponding attestation and declaration to Mr. Krlic's statement. So the Prosecution is simply asking for the Chamber to review its decision and perhaps clarify it for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I can deal with that very quickly, Mr. Groome. I read the following for you: On the 23rd of September, the Chamber issued its decision on the Prosecution's 18th motion pursuant to Rule 92 bis. In the disposition, the Chamber instructed the Prosecution to file an attestation and declaration in relation to the 27th of June, 1996, witness statement of Mirsad Krlic and the supplemental information sheet of the 24th of April, 2005, in relation to the same witness. The Chamber wishes to clarify that it is not necessary for the attestation and declarations to be filed in relation to Witness Krlic as the Chamber had already deemed as sufficient the attestation provided by him in a previous case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That resolves the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution appreciates the clarification. Mr. Traldi is present in court to raise one last brief matter. And, Your Honour, can I just simply say that Ms. Hochhauser has been delayed. Something has come up and she will be here, I believe, in the next few minutes, but I will be here to take the cross-examination of Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Can we move go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Hogan? Could I ask you, Mr. Lukic, may I take it that you'll finish today at what moment approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we -- we spent some time in this session, my plan was to finish in the first two sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the first two sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But now I'm lacking 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're lacking 20 minutes, but at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the next witness will be ready to testify only on Thursday, it's for sure that we'll conclude the testimony of Mr. Hogan today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the witness is -- we're waiting for the witness. Meanwhile, I deal with a very short matter related to P1467, which was admitted into evidence with Mirko Trivic. The Chamber requests the Registry to replace the English translation of P1467 with a new version that has been uploaded into e-court under number 65 ter 25860 a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had some technical problems yesterday, so I'll try to fix it today and just ask you to put that red dot again. Hopefully it would work today.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we need -- it was accepted yesterday, but I don't know if it's in the system since it broke down. I'll ask for 1D514.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think that a number was already assigned to the marked map D376, so if the witness now marks this map that will then, once being marked, be admitted as D376.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, you're invited to, again, put the red dot --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at the place of the house where ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further marking required, Mr. Lukic? If not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then this one will be saved and is the admitted version of D376.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, may I ask you, yesterday, if I remember correctly, you put the red dot on the other site of that street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour. And I -- I -- I attempted to again this morning. However, the -- the dot is so much bigger than a house so I thought, well, it's approximately there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In your recollection is this on the right side of this street or on the left side of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From this view-point it's on the left side. It's on the west side of the street. I see it has disappeared. I can mark it again, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need to have it marked again because we could -- now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a problem. Nobody's receiving B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. The B/C/S translation is still not received.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it is apparently. What I do not fully understand is nowadays we have technological means which are so much more precise. If you take a Google Earth, you most likely would be able to spot this one single house. So, therefore, why are we working with this, if I could say, old-fashioned systems, if it comes down to one house. I would invite the parties to see whether they could get a Google Earth picture of this ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know what -- what the Defence, of course, wants to do with the blue circles and the red dot. Of course, much depends. If it's just to say it was in this area apart from that we knew that already, that it doesn't make any -- but if later on we are trying to reconstruct on the basis of maps lines of sight and whether they crossed over a cemetery or not, then why not use the most precise technical means?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, once the witness is released as a witness we will ask Mr. Hogan to look at Google Earth and see if the house is still there, it's in the same location, and, if so, I'll negotiate with Mr. Lukic about doing that. I was going to suggest for our purposes today could we not just zoom in on that portion of the map and allow Mr. Hogan to put a more precise mark. And, finally, Your Honours, to remind the Chamber of something I said at the start of the case, the Prosecution does have a very sophisticated mapping programme which allows the calculation of lines of sight elevations. It is very precise. It's, I think, the state-of-the-art technology. So if the Chamber or the Defence ever want to -- to look at it and rely or -- or explore the possible use of it in the trial, the Prosecution would make the arrangements to make that happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, a lot of offers to improve the accuracy of your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We were just being reminded how OTP is powerful and we are not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic, Google Earth is not something so special that I might even attempt to get you the Google Earth picture of that specific area during the break. Takes me five minute, approximately, but it has got nothing to do with resources. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, just to be sure, D376 has been -- is now saved and is in the body of evidence as admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The initial document 1D00514 has -- that was assigned D376 has been replaced with the new document, as marked by the witness [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now we have the unmarked version still on our screen. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now I'd like to have 1D515 in the e-court, please. If we could zoom in a bit more the middle of the picture. Bit more. And just bit more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this photograph, sir, we see in the centre, a bit to the right from the centre, a part of the Muslim cemetery we spoke about yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to make that out, but I wouldn't be surprised. I can see it a little bit more clearly now, and I think it might be part of the cemetery, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you put a circle around the place where you see this part of the cemetery, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have this exhibit -- we would like to tender it [overlapping speakers] evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, photograph marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D377, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we could now have D377 on one part -- side of the screen, and beside it, to have 1D516.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This looks in the same direction, only the lens is turned a bit sideways, and it was photographed from outside the house where the incident happened; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about the view from the location where the little girl was shot, this shows a different angle. This -- what we're looking at does not look in the same direction towards Baba Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were on the spot, were you able to see this cemetery?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that I noticed the cemetery from the porch or from the entrance-way of the witness's house, victim witness's house. I -- we had to zoom in quite a bit for me to see what looked like headstones on that photograph just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have then D377 back on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It takes just a little bit of time for it to be uploaded. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's easier to use the unmarked version with the 1D number --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- 514. If you want to compare the two, it's perhaps not necessary to have the marked version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's only -- yeah -- thank you, Your Honour. It's only 1D515, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, Mr. Hogan, we see - can you see it now? - this cemetery we discussed?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After -- after we had zoomed in and I can see the un-zoomed part, I can make it out, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll need that picture on our screens. Okay. Now we have ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the marked photograph was a zoomed-in version of the photograph produced by the Defence, which makes less clear that the position from where the photograph was taken is at least different from the position taken at the time by Mr. Hogan, who said that he had taken that picture from the position; that is, place and the height of the lens adapted to a small child. And, therefore, Mr. Lukic, of course, the Chamber will ask itself what is the use of saying that there is a line of sight to a point different from the point where the victim was hit. So if you would please keep that in mind when further developing your Defence position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Can we have D125, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a photograph that you took; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember if it was -- I personally took it or my colleague took it, but I was present, one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, thank you. [Interpretation] Could you mark on this photograph the location of Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the record is clear and so that I understand what we're looking at, although Mr. Lukic is mentioned that it is a photo, and I agree with that, it appears to be some black markings on it. So the record should reflect that is already marked but -- and Mr. Lukic could enlighten me as to what those markings are. I certainly would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads "baba," if I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And obviously it's marked by Ms. Fatima Pita. It says at the left part of this picture, on 25th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do we need those markings, Mr. Lukic, because, if not, we'd rather use a -- a -- an unmarked photograph. But ... I don't know what you're -- what you're heading for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's -- that's the only photo we have. That's why we used marked version. I would like to have clean version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But then please put your questions. If the Prosecution could find -- try to find whether there's a blank version. But it may not influence ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not marked the photograph as yet. But do you wish me to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if we can -- if there is no any unmarked version of this picture, if we can save this one as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Photograph previously marked, now marked by the witness, Madam Registrar, would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D378, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, Mr. Hogan, did you know, and do you know today, that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina controlled the area of the cemetery; in fact, the entire area up to Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were on the ground. Do you agree that the cemetery is approximately halfway between the site of the incident and Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably a third. But I -- I hadn't measured it so I will not dispute approximately half, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you establish the distance from the site of the incident to Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Actually, the sniping expert established the distance and I was standing beside him, and I do not recall what exactly it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, on that occasion, you did not only rely on what the mother, Fatima Pita, and the father, Ekrem Pita, told you about the distance to Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not only rely on them, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you establish on that occasion if there was optical visibility of the house from the cemetery we have just seen?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because we could not see the cemetery from the location from which the -- where the little girl was standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your question was whether there was "optical visibility of the house from the cemetery we have just seen." Did you mean to say the cemetery we just have seen or a line of visibility we have just seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cemetery. Just cemetery. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you establish whether the same trees existed in the year of the incident - let me see, 13th December 1992 - and at the moment when you were on the site?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked about the tree that was growing between the witness's house and the next-door house that we saw circled in the black in the -- the previous photograph. But we did not establish the growth of the other trees in the immediate area of the victim's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what did you establish about the tree that you made inquiries about?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That that had been planted and grown since the incident occurred, so between the time of the shooting and the time of the photograph showing the tree, and -- which is the reason that the witness circled it in black during her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we began discussing GOFRS. Let me just tell you that on transcript page in our trial 1817, lines 15 through 12 [as interpreted], and page 1803, line 14, up to 1804, line 1, Mr. John Jordan explained that GOFRS were located on the site related to the incident F12, where fire was opened at Dzenana Sokolovic and her 7-year-old son, Nermin Divovic, while they were walking along Zmaja od Bosne Street. Did you deal with this at all, and did you establish how far the members and the vehicles of the GOFRS were from the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were parked in their vehicle within 50 metres of the UNPROFOR APC, as far as I can recall. And I'm getting my information from the video and from my previous interview with Mr. Jordan and his previous testimony in another trial. And I'm -- the -- the figure of 50 metres sort of sticks in my mind, within 50 metres of the UNPROFOR APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding this incident, F12, Mr. van der Weijden maintained on page 6538 and -39, the transcript of this trial, that the co-ordinates you determined were not accurate, at least not the co-ordinates that he received from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see on the screens page 6539. [In English] can we see our transcript or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number. It's unclear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page of transcript, 6539.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is it uploaded in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not. But before we were able to see our transcript, even if it's not uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are talking about our transcript, in our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart also informs that she can show in Sanction, if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It can be shown by Madam Registrar as well, although this is not the usual way we operate, Mr. Lukic. And, of course, everyone in this courtroom, apart from Sanction, can have a look at transcript from any day in e-court. So if you have the day and if you just intend to read from it, because you can't, then automatically have it admitted, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We need the date also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, which witness? Mr. van der Weijden, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's January 10th of 2013. And, again, Ms. Stewart has the passage right on the screen if that's [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... okay, then if Ms. Stewart would assist us, then that would be appreciated. Could we have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need line 9 to line 14. And I will read. I quote: "Q. Okay.
